title: Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Risk Stratification and Discharge versus Admission

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult acute lower GI bleeding triage, Oakland risk assessment and hospital disposition from the BSG guideline.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national LGIB guideline was opened.
SFDA status is not applicable because this topic does not prescribe a medicine.

pathophysiology.summary: Colonic or anorectal bleeding presents as fresh or altered blood per rectum. Ongoing blood loss can reduce circulating volume and oxygen delivery. Haemodynamic instability may reflect brisk upper rather than lower GI bleeding. Antithrombotic therapy can increase severity and recurrence.
keyMechanisms: Colonic or anorectal bleeding presents as fresh or altered blood per rectum.
Ongoing blood loss can reduce circulating volume and oxygen delivery.
Haemodynamic instability may reflect brisk upper rather than lower GI bleeding.
Antithrombotic therapy can increase severity and recurrence.

symptoms: Fresh or dark red rectal bleeding, dizziness, syncope, abdominal pain or change in bowel habit.
physicalSigns: Tachycardia, hypotension, pallor, abdominal tenderness, rectal blood or melaena.
redFlags: Shock index above 1 after initial resuscitation, ongoing major bleeding, syncope, peritonism, severe anaemia or anticoagulation-related concern.
precipitants: Diverticular disease, anorectal disease, colitis, neoplasia, angiodysplasia and antithrombotic therapy.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Haemodynamic instability, melaena, peptic history or raised urea-to-creatinine pattern; consider upper endoscopy if CTA is normal.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Age, sex, prior LGIB admission, rectal findings, heart rate, systolic BP and haemoglobin
ruleIn.expectedFinding: 8 or lower may support discharge; above 8 is major bleeding
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use only after clinical assessment; the guideline notes validation was outside Saudi Arabia.

clinicalManagement.title: Initial assessment
actions: Assess airway, circulation, IV access and haemodynamic response; calculate shock index after initial resuscitation.
Perform abdominal and rectal examination and obtain full blood count, renal profile, coagulation testing and group-and-save/crossmatch according to severity.

clinicalManagement.title: Risk stratify
actions: Calculate Oakland score for stable, self-terminating bleeding.
Admit major bleeds and patients with another clinical or social indication for admission.

clinicalManagement.title: Localise ongoing major bleeding
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Urgently when unstable or active bleeding suspected
actions: Obtain CT angiography when shock index remains above 1 or active bleeding is suspected.
Coordinate endoscopic, interventional-radiology or surgical haemostasis based on the source and response.

medicationPlan.note: This pathway does not initiate a medicine; anticoagulant and antiplatelet interruption or reversal requires indication-specific specialist and local protocol review.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Oakland score 8 or lower and no other indication for admission.

teaching.scope: Adult acute lower GI bleeding triage, Oakland risk assessment and hospital disposition from the BSG guideline.
learningObjectives: Separate stable minor bleeding from major bleeding.
Use CTA promptly for ongoing unstable bleeding.
pitfalls: Using the Oakland score without clinical judgement.
Delaying CTA in ongoing unstable bleeding.
keyPoints: Oakland 8 or lower supports discharge only when no other admission indication exists.
Unstable apparent LGIB may arise above the ligament of Treitz.

patientEducation: Explain recurrence signs and when to return immediately.
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid non-prescribed NSAIDs and maintain hydration while awaiting review unless restricted.
mdtReferrals: Gastroenterology, interventional radiology, surgery, transfusion service and anticoagulation team as needed.
dischargeCriteria: Self-terminating minor bleed, Oakland score 8 or lower, no other admission indication, reliable urgent outpatient investigation and clear return advice.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Arrange urgent outpatient lower-GI investigation and communicate antithrombotic plans to the responsible prescriber.
